body.statement: Fix the two-arm schedule \(x^{(2)}\), its common-denominator marginals \(F^{(2)}\), positive counts \(m_0+m_1=N\), the zero-sum contrast \(d\), and the complete-randomization law for \(Z^{(2)}\). Every extreme point of \(\Gamma(F^{(2)})\) is representable by a table in \(\mathcal S_N(F^{(2)})\). Consequently \(\min_{\pi\in\Gamma(F^{(2)})}\int(d_0y_0+d_1y_1)^2\,d\pi=\min_{T\in\mathcal S_N(F^{(2)})}N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N(d_0T_{0i}+d_1T_{1i})^2=C_{\mathrm{co}}^{(2)}(F^{(2)})\), while \(\max_{\pi\in\Gamma(F^{(2)})}\int(d_0y_0+d_1y_1)^2\,d\pi=\max_{T\in\mathcal S_N(F^{(2)})}N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N(d_0T_{0i}+d_1T_{1i})^2=C_{\mathrm{ctr}}^{(2)}(F^{(2)})\). The estimator \(\widehat\theta_N^{(2)}\) is design-unbiased for \(\theta_N^{(2)}\), and, as \(x^{(2)}\) ranges over \(\mathcal S_N(F^{(2)})\), the sharp interval hull of \(\operatorname{Var}_{Z^{(2)}}(\widehat\theta_N^{(2)})\) is exactly \([L_N^{(2)}(F^{(2)}),U_N^{(2)}(F^{(2)})]\). In particular, \(U_N^{(2)}=\sum_b d_b^2S_b^{2,(2)}/m_b-[\sum_b d_b^2S_b^{2,(2)}+2d_0d_1\overline S_{10}^{(2)}]/N\) and \(L_N^{(2)}=\sum_b d_b^2S_b^{2,(2)}/m_b-[\sum_b d_b^2S_b^{2,(2)}+2d_0d_1\underline S_{10}^{(2)}]/N\), which are the Aronow--Green--Lee (2014, Lemma 1 and equations (7)--(11)) sharp endpoints for the scaled difference in means.
body.justification: The bivariate reduction is the required sanity check and isolates the loss of Birkhoff integrality as a genuinely three-arm phenomenon.
body.gap: Aronow, Green, and Lee (2014) solve the two-arm endpoint exactly; the proposal preserves their result as the zero-gap boundary rather than replacing its estimand.
body.consumer: Existing two-arm trial workflows remain unchanged, while software can activate the realization certificate only for three or more arms.
